result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers suggest a wall printout for Thursday and a short deck with an ask for the execs. B builds the exec version around 2–3 marked moments and ties each idea to its moment through hypotheses. A gives separate slides for grouped pain points and prioritized ideas, without linking ideas to moments. B is less practical: it is longer and starts redesigning the map with rules for cell wording, stage names and the emotion line. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A ties each idea to a specific moment through its hypothesis format, says plainly what to cut (the rest of the grid, the ideas on hold) and ends on a concrete ask. B splits moments, pain-point themes and ideas onto separate slides, so ideas aren't attached to the moments they fix. However, A drifts into redesigning the map (renaming stages, changing the emotion curve to named feelings, adding framing and status strips), which B avoids.
